subject: Security questionnaire — Tensile
facts: Northwind security review conducted May 2026, ahead of the June requirements thread
Tensile has no SOC 2 report; observation window starts October 2026
Review flagged SSO and audit log export as gaps
Karin Holt is Information Security at Northwind Logistics
body:
## Message 1 — 19 May 2026, 14:33

**From:** Karin Holt <karin.holt@northwindlogistics.com>
**To:** Dana Whitfield <dana@tensile.dev>
**Cc:** Linda Marsh <linda.marsh@northwindlogistics.com>
**Subject:** Security questionnaire — Tensile

Dana,

Attached is our standard vendor security questionnaire. We run this annually against every vendor with access to production telemetry, and Tensile is in scope this year because usage has grown past our internal threshold.

Sections 1 through 6 are the usual — encryption, key management, incident response, subprocessors. Section 7 covers access control and section 9 covers audit and logging. Those two tend to be where smaller vendors have gaps, so start there if you're triaging.

We'd like it back within two weeks if that's workable.

Karin Holt
Information Security, Northwind Logistics

---

## Message 2 — 26 May 2026, 18:02

**From:** Dana Whitfield <dana@tensile.dev>
**To:** Karin Holt <karin.holt@northwindlogistics.com>
**Cc:** Linda Marsh <linda.marsh@northwindlogistics.com>
**Subject:** Re: Security questionnaire — Tensile

Karin,

Completed questionnaire attached. I've answered everything honestly, including where we fall short, because I'd rather you find the gaps from me than from the document.

The parts you'll care about:

**Encryption and key management** — AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit, keys in AWS KMS with annual rotation. No concerns here.

**Incident response** — documented process, 24-hour customer notification commitment. We've had one Sev-1 in the last twelve months, disclosed at the time.

**Section 7, access control** — this is a gap. We support individual accounts with enforced MFA, but we do not support SAML or any external identity provider today. Every user authenticates directly against us.

**Section 9, audit and logging** — partial. We log access events and retain them for ninety days internally, but there is no customer-facing export and no configurable retention.

**SOC 2** — we don't have a report. We've selected an auditor and the Type II observation window starts in October, which puts a report roughly mid-2027.

I'd rather set expectations correctly than have this come back as a surprise in six months.

Dana Whitfield
CTO, Tensile

---

## Message 3 — 27 May 2026, 09:50

**From:** Karin Holt <karin.holt@northwindlogistics.com>
**To:** Dana Whitfield <dana@tensile.dev>
**Cc:** Linda Marsh <linda.marsh@northwindlogistics.com>
**Subject:** Re: Security questionnaire — Tensile

Dana,

Appreciated — that's a more useful response than most.

Assessment: no blocking findings for continued use this term. Two items go on our remediation register.

1. **Federated identity (SAML).** Our tenant-wide Okta consolidation completes at the end of Q3. Vendors without SAML get written up in the quarterly access audit from that point.
2. **Audit log export.** Twelve months retention, customer-initiated, machine-readable.

The absent SOC 2 is noted but not blocking given the compensating controls you've described.

Linda will pick up timelines with your commercial team — this is a requirements conversation now, not a security one.

Karin

subject: Tensile — June update

Northwind renewal flagged as a risk
body:
**From:** Ravi Menon <ravi@tensile.dev>
**To:** investors@tensile.dev
**Date:** 6 July 2026, 09:05
**Subject:** Tensile — June update

Everyone,

Softer month than the last four, and I want to be straight about why.

**Metrics**

- ARR: $940,000 (+9.3% MoM)
- MRR: $78,300
- Net burn: $181,000
- Cash: $1.72M
- Runway: 9 months
- Customers: 56
- Team: 13

**What went well**

Q2 board meeting on 18 June. We approved the Series A raise formally and set a target of $12M.

First conversation with Aster Ventures on 4 June went well — James has spent real time in this category and asked better questions than most. Several other conversations in flight.

Tracing GA work is on schedule for Q3.

**What didn't**

Growth decelerated to 9.3% from an average of about 11.5% over the previous three months. Two things caused it, and neither is a surprise once you look.

First, only one of the two deals that slipped from May actually closed in June. The other is still in security review.

Second, self-serve conversion dipped back to 5.4% after a pricing page change we made mid-month. We've reverted it.

Separately, and more concerning than either: our largest account, Northwind, has enterprise requirements tied to their renewal at the end of September. We are working through what that means. I'd rather flag it now than in the September update.

**Asks**

Introductions to funds that lead at $10-15M. We have good conversations going but I'd like more shots on goal before we're in a position where we need one of them to say yes.

Ravi Menon
CEO, Tensile

Thanks as always,

CEO, Tensile

**From:** Ravi Menon <ravi@tensile.dev>
**To:** Priya Kothari <priya@fernpath.vc>
**Subject:** Re: Tensile — term sheet

Priya,

Received, thank you. Genuinely pleased.

Give me until Monday to go through it properly with Dana and with Nadia. One thing I can flag now — the 12% pool coming out of pre-money is doing a lot of quiet work, and I'd like to talk about that specifically rather than have it be the thing we discover we disagree about in week three.

## Message 3 — 27 July 2026, 11:32

**From:** Ravi Menon <ravi@tensile.dev>
**To:** Priya Kothari <priya@fernpath.vc>
**Subject:** Re: Tensile — term sheet

Priya,

Three things, in order of how much I care.

**Option pool.** 12% pre-money is effectively a $6M valuation adjustment dressed as an operational number. We have a hiring plan for the next eighteen months — Head of Engineering, three engineers, two on the commercial side. That plan needs about 6.5%. Even with room for error, 12% is more than we can defend. I'd like to land at 10%.

**Board.** No issue with the seat. I would like us to commit to filling the independent seat within six months of close rather than leaving it open indefinitely. We've had it vacant since the seed and it hasn't served us well.

**Preference and anti-dilution.** No objection, both are as expected.

Everything else I'm comfortable with.

Ravi

**From:** Priya Kothari <priya@fernpath.vc>
**To:** Ravi Menon <ravi@tensile.dev>
**Subject:** Re: Tensile — term sheet

Ravi,

Reasonable on all three.

Pool: we can go to 10.5%. Below that I'd be arguing with my own partnership about a hiring plan I can't underwrite, and I'd rather spend that credibility on something else.

Board: happy to write the six-month commitment into the docs. Agreed it shouldn't sit empty.

Preference and anti-dilution stand as drafted.

If 10.5% works, sign and we'll start diligence Monday. I'd like reference calls in the first two weeks — customers, and two of your investors.

**To:** Priyanka Rao <p.rao@caldersystems.com>
**Subject:** Re: SOC 2 timeline

Priyanka,

Honest answer: auditor selected, Type II observation window starts in October. That's a twelve month window, so a report lands around mid-2027.

I know that's later than you'd like. What I can offer in the meantime is our completed security questionnaire and last November's penetration test summary, which covers most of what your compliance team is actually trying to establish.

Happy to get on a call with them directly if that's easier.

Marcus

**From:** Marcus Oyelaran <marcus@tensile.dev>
**To:** Priyanka Rao <p.rao@caldersystems.com>
**Subject:** Calder renewal — early conversation

Priyanka,

Your renewal is 1 January, which feels far away but our finance year-end planning happens in October, so I'd rather have the conversation now.

Current is $62,000. I'd expect to propose an increase, but I want to understand your plans before putting a number on it — are you expecting to add teams next year?

Marcus

---

## Message 2 — 5 August 2026, 10:20

**From:** Priyanka Rao <p.rao@caldersystems.com>
**To:** Marcus Oyelaran <marcus@tensile.dev>
**Subject:** Re: Calder renewal — early conversation

Marcus,

Yes, two more teams, probably January. That's roughly twenty more engineers.

Two things that affect whether it happens on time.

First, the SLA amendment takes effect 1 October and I'll want to see a clean quarter against it before I expand.

Second, access management. Right now every engineer authenticates individually and I'm approving accounts by hand. At twenty more people that becomes untenable. I raised this in May and I don't think anything's changed.

Priyanka

**From:** Dana Whitfield <dana@tensile.dev>
**To:** Linda Marsh <linda.marsh@northwindlogistics.com>
**Subject:** Re: Webhook deliveries failing

Linda,

Found it. Your endpoint started returning 429s on Tuesday and our retry logic gives up after five attempts, then disables the webhook silently. The silent part is our bug — you should have been told.

Re-enabled. I've raised a fix so that a disabled webhook sends an email rather than just stopping.

Sev-3, single customer. No postmortem but it's in the log.

Dana
